content.name: Oliver Mensah
content.title: Primary Care Network Clinical Pharmacist (Independent Prescriber)
content.summary: GPhC-registered pharmacist and independent prescriber with nine years in community pharmacy and general practice. I now run respiratory and polypharmacy clinics across a five-practice PCN, where structured medication reviews saved an estimated £61,000 in prescribing costs last year.

experience.title: Pre-registration Pharmacist
bullets: Completed the 52-week pre-registration year across two busy community branches dispensing 6,000 items a month.
Delivered 150 New Medicine Service consultations and 80 Medicines Use Reviews under supervision.
Passed the GPhC registration assessment at the first attempt.

experience.title: Pharmacist Manager
bullets: Managed a 100-hour pharmacy with 7 staff, accountable for clinical governance, controlled drugs and a monthly script volume of 9,500 items.
Grew NHS service income by 35% by expanding flu vaccination, NMS and the Community Pharmacist Consultation Service.
Ran Covid-19 vaccination sessions at a local hub, vaccinating over 3,000 patients in four months.
Achieved a 'standards met' outcome at the GPhC inspection with no improvement actions.

experience.title: PCN Clinical Pharmacist
bullets: Carry out around 60 structured medication reviews a month for patients with polypharmacy, frailty or care-home residence across five GP practices.
Run independent prescribing clinics for asthma and COPD, switching 240 patients to lower-carbon inhalers where clinically appropriate.
Reduced high-risk NSAID and antiplatelet prescribing combinations by 38% through searches in EMIS and targeted recalls.
Supervise two trainee pharmacy technicians and support the PCN's new foundation trainee pharmacist placements.

education.school: University of the West of England

achievements.title: GPhC registered pharmacist
achievements.detail: Registered with the General Pharmaceutical Council since 2018; annotated as an independent prescriber since 2022.

achievements.title: Prescribing savings
achievements.detail: Medication reviews and switches saved an estimated £61,000 across the PCN in 2025.
